raw_case_text: An antiretroviral therapy (ART)-naive woman was asymptomatic for tuberculosis (TB) at presentation and started on first-line ART (see Table 1 for more information). She rapidly deteriorated and presented again after 10 days with night sweats, a cough, and abdominal pain. She met the criteria for AlereLAM testing on this date, which revealed a strongly positive (4+) result. The patient was placed onto TB treatment and sputum was sent for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and mycobacterial culture, along with urine for mycobacterial culture.

subjective.chief_complaint: An adult female presenting with acute clinical deterioration, cough, night sweats, and abdominal pain ten days after commencing antiretroviral therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, initially asymptomatic for active opportunistic infections, commenced first-line antiretroviral therapy. Within 10 days of ART initiation, she experienced rapid clinical deterioration characterized by the onset of persistent cough, drenching night sweats, and severe abdominal pain, prompting urgent medical re-evaluation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Newly diagnosed chronic retroviral illness, previously antiretroviral therapy (ART)-naive prior to commencing first-line regimen 10 days earlier.
subjective.review_of_systems: Cough, drenching night sweats, and abdominal pain; denies hemoptysis or focal neurologic deficits.

objective.physical_examination: Acutely unwell female meeting clinical criteria for severe illness and lateral flow screening; detailed vital signs not documented in raw text.
objective.routine_investigations: Sputum and urine samples collected and submitted for mycobacterial culture and specialized diagnostic antigen screening.
objective.advanced_workup: Sputum submitted for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra molecular testing.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis unmasked as tuberculosis-associated immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (TB-IRIS) following initiation of first-line antiretroviral therapy for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. Diagnostic confirmation: Strongly positive (4+) urine lipoarabinomannan (AlereLAM) lateral flow test, supported by diagnostic workup with sputum Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and concurrent sputum and urine mycobacterial cultures. Plan & Outcome: Promptly commenced on standard weight-based antitubercular therapy while continuing clinical monitoring and antiretroviral management.
